input_bundle_canonicalization: Sort paths by ordinal repository-relative path; for each input encode path, one TAB, lowercase SHA-256, one LF as UTF-8; concatenate records and SHA-256 the result.

modeled_claims.claim: Finite asynchronous replicated round and certificate state transitions preserve safety for the declared TLC scopes, including the mandatory f=1 configuration.
Durable context-bound votes, quorum formation, view change and certified abort do not permit conflicting finalized bodies within the declared Byzantine bound.
Ticket, lease, commitment, availability, input-close, ISC and seed ordering obey immutable parent and close-policy rules.
EC/APC, parameter shard, aggregate root, ApplyQC and current-pointer transitions preserve exact certificate parentage and complete coverage.

Crash, restart, journal recovery, replay, partition, logical deadlines, artifact loss, exact repair, blocking and certified abort preserve the parent current checkpoint unless a valid ApplyQC advances it.

Consensus-visible arithmetic is bounded integer or exact rational arithmetic; finite boundary behavior is model checked and parametric quorum, accumulator, hierarchy, coverage and apply claims are theorem obligations.
Only allowlisted certified global immutable objects can enter the abstract distribution publication set.
Later implementations can project protocol-visible executions onto the stable formal action and trace vocabulary, with documented internal stuttering only.

non_modeled_claims.claim: No proof of hash, signature, canonical-serialization or CAS implementations; only their named abstractions and correct context binding are modeled.
No permissionless identity, Sybil-resistance, economic-incentive or key-management security proof.
No proof that workers execute ML training honestly and no universal poisoning or backdoor resistance guarantee.
No convergence, model-quality, compression-quality, WAN-performance, memory-footprint or scalability achievement claim.
TLC does not prove unbounded nodes, messages or values; theorem results cover only their exact stated parametric abstractions and preconditions.

Optional worker-local quantization residuals, peer scheduling/backpressure/filesystem defenses and capability benchmarking are concrete later-feature obligations outside the core consensus state model.
No safety claim applies after more than f validators are Byzantine or the unforgeable identity/signature abstraction fails.
Trace refinement and conformance fixtures do not constitute a full general proof of arbitrary implementation code, cryptography or platform behavior.

mandatory_assumptions: For safety, each validator epoch has exactly 3f+1 unique validators and at most f are Byzantine.
Honest validators persist vote intent before transmitting a signature and never sign conflicting bodies in one vote context.
Hashes, signatures, identities and canonical encodings satisfy the named abstractions.
Liveness is claimed only per config under explicit eventual synchrony, honest responsive quorum, artifact availability or repairability, bounded computation and declared fairness.
Every theorem-backed runtime transition separately validates and content-addresses the concrete theorem preconditions.
